1→# Gmail Skill - Detailed Usage Guide 2→ 3→Token-efficient Gmail management through CLI scripts for Claude Code. 4→ 5→## Quick Start 6→ 7→All scripts are in the `scripts/` directory and output JSON. 8→ 9→## gmail-send.js - Send Emails 10→ 11→Send emails with support for HTML, CC/BCC, and custom headers. 12→ 13→### Basic Usage 14→```bash 15→node gmail-send.js --to "user@example.com" --subject "Hello" --body "Message body" 16→``` 17→ 18→### Advanced Options 19→```bash 20→node gmail-send.js \ 21→ --to "user@example.com" \ 22→ --cc "cc@example.com" \ 23→ --bcc "bcc@example.com" \ 24→ --subject "Project Update" \ 25→ --body "The project is complete." \ 26→ --reply-to "reply@example.com" 27→``` 28→ 29→### HTML Email 30→```bash 31→node gmail-send.js \ 32→ --to "user@example.com" \ 33→ --subject "Newsletter" \ 34→ --html "

Welcome

This is HTML content

" 35→``` 36→ 37→### Output 38→```json 39→{ 40→ "success": true, 41→ "messageId": "18d1234567890", 42→ "threadId": "18d1234567890", 43→ "to": "user@example.com", 44→ "subject": "Hello" 45→} 46→``` 47→ 48→## gmail-search.js - Search Emails 49→ 50→Search emails using Gmail's powerful query syntax. 51→ 52→### Basic Search 53→```bash 54→node gmail-search.js --query "is:unread" --limit 10 55→``` 56→ 57→### Search Operators 58→```bash 59→# From specific sender 60→node gmail-search.js --query "from:boss@company.com" 61→ 62→# Emails with attachments 63→node gmail-search.js --query "has:attachment" 64→ 65→# Date range 66→node gmail-search.js --query "after:2024/01/01 before:2024/12/31" 67→ 68→# Subject search 69→node gmail-search.js --query "subject:invoice" 70→ 71→# Combine operators 72→node gmail-search.js --query "from:client@example.com has:attachment is:unread" 73→ 74→# Complex search 75→node gmail-search.js --query "is:important OR is:starred" --limit 20 76→``` 77→ 78→### Output 79→```json 80→{ 81→ "success": true, 82→ "count": 3, 83→ "total": 150, 84→ "query": "is:unread", 85→ "messages": [ 86→ { 87→ "id": "18d1234567890", 88→ "threadId": "18d1234567890", 89→ "from": "sender@example.com", 90→ "to": "you@gmail.com", 91→ "subject": "Project Update", 92→ "date": "Mon, 15 Jan 2024 10:30:00 -0800", 93→ "snippet": "The project is progressing well...", 94→ "labels": ["INBOX", "UNREAD"] 95→ } 96→ ] 97→} 98→``` 99→ 100→## gmail-read.js - Read Messages 101→ 102→Read full message content and thread details. 103→ 104→### Read Single Message 105→```bash 106→node gmail-read.js --id "18d1234567890" 107→``` 108→ 109→### Read Message with Thread Context 110→```bash 111→node gmail-read.js --id "18d1234567890" --thread 112→``` 113→ 114→### Output 115→```json 116→{ 117→ "success": true, 118→ "id": "18d1234567890", 119→ "threadId": "18d1234567890", 120→ "from": "sender@example.com", 121→ "to": "you@gmail.com", 122→ "subject": "Project Update", 123→ "date": "Mon, 15 Jan 2024 10:30:00 -0800", 124→ "labels": ["INBOX", "UNREAD"], 125→ "snippet": "The project is progressing well...", 126→ "body": "Full email body content here..." 127→} 128→``` 129→ 130→## gmail-labels.js - Manage Labels 131→ 132→List, create, add, and remove labels. 133→ 134→### List All Labels 135→```bash 136→node gmail-labels.js --action list 137→``` 138→ 139→### Create New Label 140→```bash 141→node gmail-labels.js --action create --name "Project Alpha" 142→``` 143→ 144→### Add Label to Message 145→```bash 146→# Using label name 147→node gmail-labels.js --action add --id "18d1234567890" --label "Important" 148→ 149→# Using label ID 150→node gmail-labels.js --action add --id "18d1234567890" --label "Label_123" 151→``` 152→ 153→### Remove Label from Message 154→```bash 155→node gmail-labels.js --action remove --id "18d1234567890" --label "Important" 156→``` 157→ 158→### Output (list) 159→```json 160→{ 161→ "success": true, 162→ "action": "list", 163→ "count": 15, 164→ "labels": [ 165→ { 166→ "id": "INBOX", 167→ "name": "INBOX", 168→ "type": "system" 169→ }, 170→ { 171→ "id": "Label_123", 172→ "name": "Project Alpha", 173→ "type": "user" 174→ } 175→ ] 176→} 177→``` 178→ 179→## gmail-drafts.js - Manage Drafts 180→ 181→Create, update, send, and delete draft emails. 182→ 183→### List Drafts 184→```bash 185→node gmail-drafts.js --action list --limit 10 186→``` 187→ 188→### Create Draft 189→```bash 190→node gmail-drafts.js \ 191→ --action create \ 192→ --to "user@example.com" \ 193→ --subject "Draft Subject" \ 194→ --body "Draft body text" 195→``` 196→ 197→### Update Draft 198→```bash 199→node gmail-drafts.js \ 200→ --action update \ 201→ --id "r-1234567890" \ 202→ --to "user@example.com" \ 203→ --subject "Updated Subject" \ 204→ --body "Updated body text" 205→``` 206→ 207→### Send Draft 208→```bash 209→node gmail-drafts.js --action send --id "r-1234567890" 210→``` 211→ 212→### Delete Draft 213→```bash 214→node gmail-drafts.js --action delete --id "r-1234567890" 215→``` 216→ 217→### Output (create) 218→```json 219→{ 220→ "success": true, 221→ "action": "create", 222→ "draftId": "r-1234567890", 223→ "to": "user@example.com", 224→ "subject": "Draft Subject" 225→} 226→``` 227→ 228→## Common Workflows 229→ 230→### 1. Find and Reply to Unread Emails 231→```bash 232→# Search for unread emails 233→node gmail-search.js --query "is:unread" --limit 5 > /tmp/unread.json 234→ 235→# Read first message 236→MESSAGE_ID=$(cat /tmp/unread.json | jq -r '.messages[0].id') 237→node gmail-read.js --id "$MESSAGE_ID" > /tmp/message.json 238→ 239→# Send reply 240→SENDER=$(cat /tmp/message.json | jq -r '.from') 241→SUBJECT=$(cat /tmp/message.json | jq -r '.subject') 242→node gmail-send.js --to "$SENDER" --subject "Re: $SUBJECT" --body "Thanks for your message!" 243→``` 244→ 245→### 2. Organize Emails by Label 246→```bash 247→# Search for project-related emails 248→node gmail-search.js --query "subject:project alpha" > /tmp/results.json 249→ 250→# Create label 251→node gmail-labels.js --action create --name "Project Alpha" 252→ 253→# Add label to each message 254→cat /tmp/results.json | jq -r '.messages[].id' | while read id; do 255→ node gmail-labels.js --action add --id "$id" --label "Project Alpha" 256→done 257→``` 258→ 259→### 3. Draft Review Workflow 260→```bash 261→# Create draft 262→node gmail-drafts.js --action create \ 263→ --to "client@example.com" \ 264→ --subject "Proposal" \ 265→ --body "Initial draft text" > /tmp/draft.json 266→ 267→DRAFT_ID=$(cat /tmp/draft.json | jq -r '.draftId') 268→ 269→# Update after review 270→node gmail-drafts.js --action update \ 271→ --id "$DRAFT_ID" \ 272→ --to "client@example.com" \ 273→ --subject "Proposal - Final" \ 274→ --body "Revised draft text" 275→ 276→# Send when ready 277→node gmail-drafts.js --action send --id "$DRAFT_ID" 278→``` 279→ 280→## Gmail Search Operators Reference 281→ 282→| Operator | Example | Description | 283→|----------|---------|-------------| 284→| `from:` | `from:user@example.com` | Emails from sender | 285→| `to:` | `to:user@example.com` | Emails to recipient | 286→| `subject:` | `subject:invoice` | Subject contains word | 287→| `has:attachment` | `has:attachment` | Has any attachment | 288→| `filename:` | `filename:pdf` | Attachment filename | 289→| `is:unread` | `is:unread` | Unread emails | 290→| `is:read` | `is:read` | Read emails | 291→| `is:starred` | `is:starred` | Starred emails | 292→| `is:important` | `is:important` | Important emails | 293→| `label:` | `label:work` | Has specific label | 294→| `after:` | `after:2024/01/01` | After date | 295→| `before:` | `before:2024/12/31` | Before date | 296→| `older_than:` | `older_than:7d` | Older than (d/m/y) | 297→| `newer_than:` | `newer_than:2d` | Newer than (d/m/y) | 298→ 299→## Error Handling 300→ 301→All scripts return JSON error objects: 302→ 303→```json 304→{ 305→ "success": false, 306→ "error": "Token not found. Run: npm run setup" 307→} 308→``` 309→ 310→Common errors: 311→- **Token not found**: Run `npm run setup` to authenticate 312→- **Invalid credentials**: Check `scripts/auth/credentials.json` 313→- **Permission denied**: Ensure Gmail API scope is granted 314→- **Message not found**: Invalid message/draft ID 315→ 316→## Tips for Claude 317→ 318→1. **Parse JSON efficiently**: Use `jq` for extracting specific fields 319→2. **Chain operations**: Save intermediate results to `/tmp/` files 320→3. **Validate IDs**: Check that message/draft IDs exist before operations 321→4. **User-friendly output**: Convert JSON to readable summaries for users 322→5. **Error handling**: Check `success` field and handle errors gracefully 323→ Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware.
